# Journal

     blocks on the source pages, not this file. -->

## 2026-10-15 — A separate package from SpaceTimeCorrelations, no shared base

Decided: CellPhases is its own package, with no common base package.
Why: SpaceTimeCorrelations computes the pooled correlation from per-frame values and needs no
IDs and no oscillation. CellPhases needs tracked agents with long tracks and one dominant
rhythm, and pulls in DSP.jl. The two share input conventions only (per-frame positions,
values, IDs; PhysiCell snapshots). Analyses that use both, such as checking that the pooled
correlation peak does not drift, belong in analysis scripts.

*From [`man/phases.md`](../man/phases.md)*

## 2026-10-15 — Physical units only; fs always passed; band required

Decided: the API takes the band as periods `(pmin, pmax)` in minutes, `trim` and `minlength`
in minutes, and `dt` in minutes per frame; frames appear only in `frames` selections and in
results. `bandpassFilter` converts to cycles per minute and always passes `fs = 1/dt`.
`band` has no default (it is a time scale of the system studied); `order = 3` does. The
filter test measures the realised response at `pmin`, `pmax` and mid-band for four frame
intervals.
Why: the prototype once built the filter without `fs`; DSP read the cutoffs as fractions of
Nyquist and passed about 200–600 minutes instead of 100–300. The spurious "upward wave" it produced
survived every pure-sine check. Taking minutes everywhere leaves no frame-based number for a
user to mistranslate.

*From [`man/phases.md`](../man/phases.md)*

## 2026-10-15 — Masking off by default

Decided: low-amplitude masking is opt-in (`mask = q`, per-track amplitude quantile).
Why: it removes ill-defined phases but biases what remains toward strongly oscillating
moments; that trade-off is the user's to make. Phase-defect (spiral core) counting was also
considered and left out of the first version.

*From [`man/phases.md`](../man/phases.md)*

## 2026-10-15 — trim and minlength derived from the band

Decided: `trim` defaults to the filter's memory and `minlength` to `2trim + 2·band[2]`, both
in minutes.
Why: the prototype fixed 18 and 90 frames for 10-minute frames and a 100–300-minute band.
Both are really properties of the filter: 18 frames was "about the filter's memory", and 90
frames "five cycles plus trim". Deriving them keeps them right when the band or the frame
interval changes. For the prototype's settings the derived values are 180 minutes (18
frames, as before) and 960 minutes (96 frames rather than 90).

*From [`man/phases.md`](../man/phases.md)*

## 2026-10-15 — PhysiCell input through cellDataSequence

Decided: the extension reads through PhysiCellOutput's `cellDataSequence` with
`include_cell_type_name = true` and filters cell types itself.
Why: `cellDataSequence` already groups each cell's values by ID across snapshots and drops
dead cells; a second reader would duplicate it.

*From [`man/physicell.md`](../man/physicell.md)*

## 2026-10-15 — Makie recipes in an extension, not MakieCore

Decided: Makie recipes live in a package extension on Makie; RecipesBase recipes stay in
core.
Why: the plan was MakieCore recipes in core, but Makie 0.24 folded MakieCore into Makie and
no longer depends on it (the last MakieCore, 0.10, pairs with Makie 0.23). Recipes written
against MakieCore would be invisible to current Makie. An extension also gets the full
Makie API, including `preferred_axis_attributes` for the rose's equal-aspect, undecorated
axis.

*From [`man/plotting.md`](../man/plotting.md)*

## 2026-10-15 — Plot data in core, recipes from it, no packaged composite

Decided: the core has plot-data functions and RecipesBase recipes built on them; no
multi-panel figure is packaged.
Why: plot data is plain numbers, so it carries no plotting dependency and serves any
package. A composite figure is an analysis choice (which signals, which panels, which cross-
check with SpaceTimeCorrelations) and stays in analysis scripts.

*From [`man/plotting.md`](../man/plotting.md)*

## 2026-10-15 — Time-shift surrogates as the null

Decided: the null for coherence and the order parameter is the time-shift surrogate, drawn
per track.
Rejected: the prototype's per-frame shuffle of phases among agents. Its mean is a fine
baseline to subtract, but consecutive frames are nearly identical, so it treats hundreds of
near-copies as independent draws and its band is far too narrow for p-values.

*From [`man/synchrony.md`](../man/synchrony.md)*

## 2026-10-15 — Speeds relative to the agents

Decided: `ω` is each agent's own phase advance, so speeds are relative to the agents.
Why: the question is how a signal travels through the tissue, not how far the tissue itself
moves. The prototype also computed a speed with one global period for all cells; per-agent ω
is the honest version and is the one kept.

*From [`man/waves.md`](../man/waves.md)*
